0.en: Comparison of Schelling's Principle of Philosophy with Fichte's
0.zh: 谢林的哲学原则与费希特的哲学原则之比较

en: It has been shown as the fundamental character of Fichte's principle that subject = object steps out of this identity and is no longer able to restore itself to the same, because the different was put into the relation of causality.
The principle of identity does not become the principle of the system; as soon as the system begins to form itself, identity is given up.
The system itself is a consistent, understanding multitude of finitudes, which is not able to gather up the original identity into the focus of totality, into absolute self-intuition.
The subject = object therefore makes itself into a subjective one, and it does not succeed in sublating this subjectivity and positing itself objectively.
zh: 作为费希特原则的基本特征已经指明：主体 = 客体从这种同一性中走出来，再也无法把自己重新恢复为这种同一性，因为差别者被置入了因果关系。
同一性的原则没有成为体系的原则；体系一开始形成，同一性就被放弃了。
体系本身是一堆前后一贯的、知性的有限物，它不能把原初的同一性收拢到总体性的焦点里，收拢成绝对的自直观。
因此主体 = 客体把自己弄成了一个主观的东西，而它没有成功扬弃这种主观性、把自己设定为客观的。

en: The principle of identity is the absolute principle of the whole of Schelling's system; philosophy and system coincide; identity does not lose itself in the parts, still less in the result.
zh: 同一性的原则是整个谢林体系的绝对原则；哲学与体系合而为一；同一性不会消失在各个部分中，更不会消失在结果中。

en: For absolute identity to be the principle of a whole system, it is necessary that subject and object both be posited as subject-object.
In Fichte's system identity has constituted itself only as a subjective subject-object.

This requires for its completion an objective subject-object, so that the absolute presents itself in each of the two, and finds itself completely only in both together, as the highest synthesis in the annihilation of both insofar as they are opposed, as their absolute point of indifference, which encloses both within itself, gives birth to both and gives birth to itself out of both.
zh: 要使绝对同一性成为一个整全体系的原则，就必须把主体和客体两者都设定为主体—客体。
在费希特的体系里，同一性只把自己建构成了一个主观的主体—客体。
这个东西为了补全自己需要一个客观的主体—客体，以致绝对者在两者中的每一个里都呈现出来，只有在这两者合在一起时才完整地找到自己，作为两者之毁灭中的最高综合——就两者相互对立而言——作为两者的绝对无差别点：这个点把两者都包含在自身中，生出两者，又从两者中生出自己。

en: If the sublation of diremption is posited as the formal task of philosophy, then reason can attempt the solution of the task in such a way that it annihilates one of the opposed and raises the other to an infinite.

This has happened in Fichte's system as far as the matter is concerned; but the opposition remains in this way, for that which is posited as absolute is conditioned by the other, and just as it subsists, the other also subsists.
In order to sublate diremption, both of the opposed, subject and object, must be sublated; they are sublated as subject and object in that they are posited as identical.
In absolute identity subject and object are related to each other and thereby annihilated; to that extent nothing is present for reflection and knowledge.

This far philosophizing goes in general, which cannot arrive at a system; it is satisfied with the negative side, which sinks everything finite into the infinite; it could well also come out again into knowledge, and it is a subjective contingency whether the need of a system is connected with it or not.
But if this negative side is itself the principle, then one is not to go out into knowledge, because every knowledge from one side at the same time enters the sphere of finitude.
It is to this intuition of the colourless light that enthusiasm holds fast; a manifoldness is in it only in that it combats the manifold.
Enthusiasm lacks consciousness of itself, that its contraction is conditioned by an expansion; it is one-sided because it itself holds fast to an opposed and makes absolute identity into an opposed.

In absolute identity subject and object are sublated; but because they are in absolute identity, they at the same time subsist, and it is this subsistence of theirs that makes a knowledge possible, for in knowledge the separation of the two is in part posited.
The separating activity is reflection; it sublates identity and the absolute insofar as it is considered for itself, and every cognition would be simply an error, because in it there is a separating.

This side, from which cognizing is a separating and its product a finite, makes every knowledge into a limited thing and thereby into a falsity; but insofar as every knowledge is at the same time an identity, to that extent there is no absolute error. — As much as identity is asserted, just as much must separation be asserted.
Insofar as identity and separation are opposed to each other, both are absolute; and if identity is to be held fast by annihilating diremption, they remain opposed to each other.

Philosophy must let the separating into subject and object have its right done to it; but in that it posits this separating as equally absolute with the identity opposed to the separation, it has posited it only conditionally, just as such an identity — which is conditioned by the annihilation of the opposed — is also only relative.
But the absolute itself is therefore the identity of identity and non-identity; opposing and being one is at the same time in it.
zh: 如果把扬弃分裂设定为哲学的形式任务，那么理性可以试着这样来解决这个任务：它毁灭对立面中的一个，把另一个提升为一个无限者。
就事情本身而言，这在费希特的体系里已经发生了；但对立以这种方式保留了下来，因为那被设定为绝对者的东西是由另一个东西制约的，而它一旦持存，另一个东西也持存。
要扬弃分裂，就必须把两个对立面、即主体和客体都扬弃；它们作为主体和客体被扬弃，是靠被设定为同一的。
在绝对同一性中，主体和客体相互关联，因而被毁灭了；就这一点而言，对反思和知识来说没有任何东西存在。
一般地从事哲学思考只能走到这一步，它无法达到一个体系；它满足于那个否定的方面，这个方面把一切有限的东西沉入无限之中；它本来也可以重新走出来达到知识，而是否有一种体系的需要与之相结合，则是一种主观的偶然性。
但如果这个否定的方面本身就是原则，那就不应当走出来达到知识，因为每一种知识都同时从一个方面进入有限性的领域。
狂热紧紧抓住这种对无色之光的直观；在它那里之所以有杂多，只是因为它同杂多作斗争。
狂热缺少对自身的意识，即它的收缩是由一种膨胀制约的；它是片面的，因为它自己固守着一个对立面，并把绝对同一性造成一个对立面。
在绝对同一性中，主体和客体是被扬弃了的；但因为它们在绝对同一性中，它们同时也持存，而正是它们的这种持存使一种知识成为可能，因为在知识中部分地设定了两者的分离。
进行分离的活动就是反思；就反思被单独考察而言，它扬弃同一性和绝对者，而每一种认识都会干脆是一种谬误，因为在认识中有一种分离。
从这一方面看，认识是一种分离、它的产物是一个有限的东西，这一方面把每一种知识都弄成一个受限制的东西，因而弄成一种虚假；但就每一种知识同时是一种同一性而言，就此而言并没有绝对的谬误。——同一性在多大程度上得到主张，分离也就必须在多大程度上得到主张。
就同一性和分离被相互对立起来而言，两者都是绝对的；而如果要用毁灭分裂的办法来固守同一性，那它们就仍然相互对立。
哲学必须让主体和客体之中的分离得到它应有的权利；但哲学既然把这种分离设定为与分离相对立的同一性同等绝对，它就只是有条件地设定了这种分离，正如这样一种同一性——它是由毁灭对立面来制约的——也只是相对的。
但绝对者本身因此就是同一性与非同一性的同一性；对立设定与合而为一在它之中同时存在。

en: In that philosophy separates, it cannot posit the separated without positing them in the absolute; for otherwise they are purely opposed, which have no other character than that the one is not insofar as the other is.

This relation to the absolute is not again a sublation of both, for then there would be no separation; rather, they are to remain as separated and not to lose this character insofar as they are posited in the absolute, or the absolute is posited in them.
And indeed both must be posited in the absolute — what right would belong to the one before the other?

Not only the same right, but the same necessity holds for both; for if only the one were related to the absolute and not the other, then their essence would be posited unequally and the unification of both, thus the task of philosophy, to sublate diremption, would be impossible.

Fichte has posited only one of the opposed into the absolute, or posited it as the absolute; the right and the necessity lie for him in self-consciousness, for only this is a self-positing, a subject = object, and this self-consciousness is not first related to the absolute as to something higher, but is itself the absolute, the absolute identity.
Its higher right to be posited as the absolute consists precisely in this, that it posits itself, whereas the object does not, which is posited solely through consciousness.

But that this position of the object is only a contingent one is evident from the contingency of the subject-object insofar as it is posited as self-consciousness; for this subject-object is itself something conditioned.

Its standpoint is therefore not the highest; it is reason posited in a limited form, and only from the standpoint of this limited form does the object appear as something not self-determining, as something absolutely determined.

Therefore both must be posited in the absolute, or the absolute in both forms, and at the same time both must subsist as separated; the subject is hereby subjective subject-object — the object objective subject-object.

And because now, since a duality is posited, each of the opposed is a self-opposed and the division goes into the infinite, so every part of the subject and every part of the object is itself in the absolute, an identity of subject and object — every cognition a truth, just as every speck of dust an organization.
zh: 哲学在作分离时，不能设定被分离者而不把它们设定在绝对者中；否则它们就是纯粹的对立面，它们的特征无非是：就另一个存在而言，这一个不存在。
这种对绝对者的关联又不是把两者扬弃，因为这样一来就没有分离了；相反，它们应当作为被分离者保持下来，并且不失去这个特征，就它们被设定在绝对者之中、或绝对者被设定在它们之中而言。
而且两者都必须被设定在绝对者中——哪一个相对另一个又有什么优先的权利呢？
两者不仅享有同样的权利，而且有同样的必然性；因为如果只有一方被关联到绝对者、另一方不是，那么它们的本质就会被不平等地设定，两者的联合、也就是哲学扬弃分裂的任务，就会不可能。
费希特只把对立面中的一个置入绝对者，或者把它设定为绝对者；在他看来，权利和必然性在于自我意识，因为只有自我意识是一种自我设定，是一个主体 = 客体，而这个自我意识并不是才被关联到作为更高者的绝对者，它本身就是绝对者，就是绝对同一性。
它具有被设定为绝对者的更高权利，恰恰就在于它自己设定自己，而客体则不然，客体只是通过意识被设定的。
但客体的这种地位只是一种偶然的地位，这一点从主体—客体的偶然性就可以看清楚，只要这个主体—客体是被设定为自我意识的；因为这个主体—客体本身是一个受制约的东西。
因此它的立场不是最高的立场，它是被设定在一种受限制的形式中的理性，而只有从这种受限制的形式的立场出发，客体才显得是一个并非自己规定自己的东西，是一个绝对被规定的东西。
因此必须把两者都置入绝对者，或者说把绝对者置入两种形式中，同时两者又作为被分离者持存；主体由此就是主观的主体—客体，——客体则是客观的主体—客体。
而且既然设定了一种二重性，对立面中的每一个就是一个自身对立的东西，分割一直延伸到无限，那么主体的每一部分和客体的每一部分本身就都在绝对者之中，都是主体与客体的同一性，——每一种认识都是一条真理，正如每一粒灰尘都是一个有机组织。

en: Only insofar as the object itself is a subject-object is I = I the absolute.
Only if the objective I is itself subject = object does I = I not turn into: I ought to be equal to I.
zh: 只有当客体本身是一个主体—客体时，我 = 我才是绝对者。
只有当客观的我本身是主体 = 客体时，我 = 我才不会变成：我应当等于我。

en: Insofar as the subject as well as the object are a subject-object, the opposition of subject and object is a real opposition; for both are posited in the absolute and thereby have reality.

The reality of the opposed and real opposition take place solely through the identity of both.46) If the object is an absolute object, then it is a merely ideal one, and the opposition is a merely ideal one as well.

Through the fact that the object is only an ideal one and is not in the absolute, the subject too becomes a merely ideal one, and such ideal factors are the I as self-positing and the not-I as opposing itself.

It avails nothing that the I is nothing but life and agility, doing and acting itself, the most real of all, the most immediate, in everyone's consciousness; as soon as it is absolutely opposed to the object, it is not something real, but only something thought, a pure product of reflection, a mere form of cognition.

And out of mere products of reflection the identity cannot construct itself as totality, for they arise through abstraction from the absolute identity, which can behave toward them immediately only destructively, not constructively.

Precisely such products of reflection are infinity and finitude, indeterminacy and determinacy, etc. From the infinite there is no transition to the finite, from the indeterminate no transition to the determinate.

The transition, as the synthesis, becomes an antinomy; but a synthesis of the finite and the infinite, of the determinate and the indeterminate, reflection, absolute separating, cannot bring about, and it is reflection that gives the law here; it has the right to assert only a formal unity, because the diremption into infinite and finite, which is its work, has been permitted and taken up; reason, however, synthesizes them in the antinomy and thereby destroys them.

If an ideal opposition is the work of reflection, which abstracts entirely from the absolute identity, then a real opposition, by contrast, is the work of reason, which posits the opposed not merely in the form of cognition but also in the form of being, identity and non-identity, as identical.
And only such a real opposition is the one in which subject and object are both posited as subject-object, both subsisting in the absolute, the absolute in both, hence reality in both.

Therefore it is only in real opposition that the principle of identity is a real principle too; if the opposition is ideal and absolute, then the identity remains a merely formal principle, it is posited only in one of the opposed forms and cannot assert itself as subject-object.

The philosophy whose principle is a formal one becomes itself a formal philosophy, just as Fichte too says somewhere47) that for God's self-consciousness - a consciousness in which through the being-posited of the I everything would be posited - his system would have only formal correctness.

If, on the other hand, the matter, the object, is itself a subject-object, then the separation of form and matter can drop away, and the system as well as its principle is no longer a merely formal one, but formal and material at once; through absolute reason everything is posited.

Only in real opposition can the absolute posit itself in the form of subject or object, can the subject pass essentially over into object or the object into subject, - the subject become itself objective, because it is originally objective or because the object is itself subject-object, or the object become subjective, because it is only originally subject-object.
Herein alone consists the true identity, that both are a subject-object, and at the same time the true opposition of which they are capable.
If both are not subject-object, then the opposition is ideal and the principle of identity is formal.

With a formal identity and an ideal opposition, no synthesis other than an incomplete one is possible, i.e. the identity, insofar as it synthesizes the opposed, is itself only a quantum, and the difference is qualitative, after the manner of the categories, in which the first, e.g. reality, is posited in the third, like the second, only quantitatively.

Conversely, however, if the opposition is real, then it is only quantitative; the principle is ideal and real at once, it is the sole quality, and the absolute, which reconstructs itself out of the quantitative difference, is not a quantum but totality.
zh: 由于主体和客体同样都是主体—客体，主体与客体的对立就是一种实在的对立；因为两者都被设定在绝对者之中，并由此具有实在性。
对立面的实在性和实在的对立，仅仅通过两者的同一性才发生。46) 如果客体是一个绝对的客体，那么它就只是一个观念物，对立也只是一个观念的对立。
由于客体只是观念的，并且不在绝对者之中，主体也就成了一个单纯的观念物，而这样一些观念的要素就是作为自我设定的我，和作为自我对立的非我。
即便自我纯粹是生命和活泼，是行动和行动本身，是每个人意识中最实在、最直接的东西，也无济于事；一旦它被绝对地与客体对立起来，它就不是实在物，而只是被思想的东西，是反思的纯粹产物，是认识的单纯形式。
而从单纯的反思产物出发，同一性无法把自己建构为总体性，因为它们产生于对绝对同一性的抽离，而绝对同一性对它们直接只能采取消灭的态度，不能采取建构的态度。
无限性和有限性、无规定性和规定性等等，正是这样的反思产物。从无限者没有向有限者的过渡，从无规定者没有向规定者的过渡。
过渡作为综合，成了一个二律背反；但有限者与无限者、规定者与无规定者的综合，反思即绝对的分割，却无法使之成立，而在这里给出法则的正是反思；反思有权只主张一种形式的统一，因为分裂为无限者和有限者——这是它的作品——已被容许并被接纳；但理性在二律背反中把它们综合起来，并由此消灭它们。
如果观念的对立是反思的作品，而反思完全抽离于绝对同一性，那么相反，实在的对立就是理性的作品，理性把对立面不仅在认识的形式中、而且在存在的形式中，把同一性和非同一性设定为同一的。
而只有这样一种实在的对立，才是这样的对立：在其中主体和客体两者都被设定为主体—客体，两者都持存于绝对者之中，两者之中都有绝对者，因而两者之中都有实在性。
因此也只有在实在的对立中，同一性的原则才是一个实在的原则；如果对立是观念的并且是绝对的，那么同一性就始终只是一个形式的原则，它只被设定在对立的形式之一中，不能把自己主张为主体—客体。
原则是形式的原则的哲学，本身会成为形式哲学，正如费希特也在某处说47)，对于上帝的自我意识——一种在其中通过我的被设定而一切都已被设定的意识——他的体系只具有形式上的正确性。
反之，如果质料、客体本身是一个主体—客体，那么形式和质料的分离就可以去掉，而体系连同它的原则就不再只是形式的，而是同时既形式又质料的；一切都是通过绝对理性被设定的。
只有在实在的对立中，绝对者才能把自己设定在主体或客体的形式中，主体才能本质上过渡为客体、或客体本质上过渡为主体，——主体才能自身成为客观的，因为它在源初就是客观的，或者因为客体本身就是主体—客体；或者客体才能成为主观的，因为它只是在源初才是主体—客体。
真正的同一性——即两者都是一个主体—客体——以及它们所能有的真正对立，只在于此。
如果两者不都是主体—客体，那么对立就是观念的，同一性的原则就是形式的。
在形式的同一性和观念的对立那里，除了不完善的综合，不可能有别的综合，也就是说，同一性在它综合对立面的范围内，本身只是一个量，而差别是质的，其方式如同诸范畴，在其中第一个范畴例如实在性，在第三个范畴里就像第二个范畴一样，只是被设定为量的。
但反过来说，如果对立是实在的，那么它就只是量的；原则同时是观念的和实在的，它是唯一的质，而从量的差别中重建自身的绝对者不是一个量，而是总体性。

en: In order to posit the true identity of subject and object, both are posited as subject-object; and each for itself is now capable of being the object of a particular science.
Each of these sciences demands abstraction from the principle of the other.

In the system of intelligence the objects are nothing in themselves, nature has only a subsistence in consciousness; abstraction is made from the fact that the object is a nature and that intelligence as consciousness is conditioned thereby.
In the system of nature it is forgotten that nature is something known; the ideal determinations which nature receives in science are at the same time immanent in it.

The mutual abstraction, however, is not a one-sidedness of the sciences, not a subjective abstraction from the real principle of the other, which would be made for the sake of knowing and would on a higher standpoint disappear to the extent that, considered in itself, the objects of consciousness, which in idealism are nothing but products of consciousness, would yet be something absolutely other and would have an absolute subsistence outside the essence of consciousness, - and on the other hand nature, which in its science is posited as self-determining and in itself ideal, considered in itself would be only object and all identity that reason recognizes in it would be only a form lent to it by knowledge.

Abstraction is made not from the inner principle but only from the peculiar form of the other science, in order to keep each pure, i.e. to preserve the inner identity of both; and the abstraction from what is peculiar to the other is an abstraction from one-sidedness.

Nature and self-consciousness are in themselves as speculation posits them in the science proper to each; they are so in themselves because it is reason that posits them, and reason posits them as subject-object, hence as the absolute, - and the only in-itself is the absolute.
It posits them as subject-object, because it is itself that produces itself as nature and as intelligence and recognizes itself in them.
zh: 为了设定主体和客体的真正同一性，两者都被设定为主体—客体；而每一个就其自身而言，从此都能够成为一门特殊科学的对象。
这些科学中的每一门都要求抽离于另一门的原则。
在智性的体系里，客体自在地什么都不是，自然界只有在意识中才持存；这里抽离掉的是：客体是自然界，而智性作为意识由此受到制约。
在自然界的体系里则忘记了：自然界是一个被知的东西；自然界在科学中获得的各种观念的规定，同时是它内在固有的。

但这种相互的抽离并不是各门科学的片面性，并不是对另一门科学的实在原则作主观的抽离——那样一种抽离是为了知识而作出的，并且在一个更高的立场上会消失到这种程度：即自在看来，意识的各种客体在观念论中不过是意识的产物，却毕竟是某种绝对他者，并且在意识的本质之外有绝对的持存；——反之，自然界在其科学中被设定为自身规定自身、并且在自身中就是观念的，而自在看来它只是客体，理性在它里面认识到的一切同一性，都只是知识借给它的一种形式。
这里抽离的不是内在的原则，而只是另一门科学的特有形式，为的是让每一门都保持纯粹，也就是说，保持两者的内在同一性；而对另一门科学特有之处的抽离，就是对片面性的抽离。
自然界和自我意识自在地就是思辨在它们各自本门科学中所设定的那样；它们之所以自在地如此，是因为设定它们的是理性，而理性把它们设定为主体—客体，也就是设定为绝对者，——而唯一的自在就是绝对者。
理性把它们设定为主体—客体，因为把自己生产为自然界和智性、并在它们之中认识自己的，正是理性本身。

en: For the sake of the true identity into which subject and object are posited, namely in that both are subject-object, and because their opposition is therefore a real one, and thus capable of passing over one into the other, the different standpoint of the two sciences is not a contradictory one.

If subject and object were absolutely opposed, only one of them the subject-object, then the two sciences could not subsist side by side in equal dignity; only the one standpoint would be the rational one.
Both sciences are possible solely through the fact that in both one and the very same [thing] is constructed in the necessary forms of its existence.
Both sciences seem to contradict each other, because in each the absolute is posited in an opposed form.

But their contradiction is not sublated by the fact that only one of them is asserted as the only science and the other is annihilated from its standpoint; the higher standpoint, which in truth sublates the one-sidedness of both sciences, is the one that cognizes the very same absolute in both.
The science of the subjective subject-object has hitherto been called transcendental philosophy; that of the objective subject-object, philosophy of nature.
Insofar as they are opposed to each other, in the former the subjective is the first, in the latter the objective.

In both, the subjective and the objective are posited in the relation of substantiality; in transcendental philosophy the subject as intelligence is the absolute substance, and nature is object, an accident, while in the philosophy of nature nature is the absolute substance, and the subject, intelligence, only an accident.

The higher standpoint is now neither one in which the one or the other science is sublated and either only the subject or only the object is asserted as the absolute, nor one in which both sciences are mixed together.
zh: 为了那真正的同一性——主体和客体被设定于其中，即两者都是主体—客体——并且因为它们的对立因此是实在的、因而一方能够过渡到另一方，两门科学各自不同的立场就不是互相矛盾的。
假如主体和客体是绝对对立的，只有一方是主体—客体，那么两门科学就不能以同等的尊严并立；只有那一个立场才会是理性的立场。
两门科学之所以可能，完全只在于：在两者中，同一个东西在其存在的必然形式中被建构出来。
两门科学看起来互相矛盾，因为在每一门中绝对者都被设定在一种对立的形式里。
但它们的矛盾并不是靠这一点扬弃的：只把其中一门主张为唯一的科学，并从它的立场出发把另一门消灭掉；真正扬弃了两门科学的片面性的那个更高立场，是在两者中认识到同一个绝对者的立场。
关于主观的主体—客体的科学至今叫做先验哲学；关于客观的主体—客体的科学叫做自然哲学。
就两者互相对立而言，在前者中主观的东西是第一位的，在后者中客观的东西是第一位的。
在两者中，主观的东西和客观的东西都被设定在实体性关系里；在先验哲学中，作为智性的主体是绝对实体，自然界是客体、是一个偶性，而在自然哲学中，自然界是绝对实体，而主体即智性只是一个偶性。
这个更高的立场如今既不是这样一种立场：在其中一门或另一门科学被扬弃，而只把主体或只把客体主张为绝对者；也不是这样一种立场：在其中两门科学被混在一起。

en: As for the mixing, what belongs to the science of nature, mixed into the system of intelligence, yields the transcendent hypotheses, which can become dazzling through a false semblance of the unification of consciousness and the unconscious; they give themselves out as natural and really do not fly beyond the palpable either, like the fibre theory of consciousness; on the other hand, what is intelligent as such, mixed into the doctrine of nature, yields the hyperphysical, especially teleological explanations.

Both blunders of mixing proceed from the tendency of explaining, for the sake of which intelligence and nature are posited in the relation of causality, the one as ground, the other as grounded, whereby however the opposition is only fixed as absolute and, through the semblance of such a formal identity as causal identity is, the way to absolute unification is completely cut off.
zh: 说到混合，属于自然科学的东西一旦被掺进智性的体系，就给出超验的假设，这些假设靠意识与无意识者之统一的假象而能使人炫目；它们自命为自然的，而且现实地也没有飞越可触知的东西，就像关于意识的纤维理论那样；反过来，智性的东西本身一旦被掺进自然学说，就给出超物理的、尤其是目的论的解释。
混合的这两种失误都出自解释的倾向，为了这种解释，智性和自然界被设定在因果性关系里，一方作为根据，另一方作为被根据的东西；但这样一来，对立只是被固定为绝对的，并且通过一种像因果同一性那样的形式同一性的假象，通往绝对统一的路被完全切断了。

en: The other standpoint, by which the contradictory element of both sciences was to be sublated, would be the one that does not let the one or the other science count as a science of the absolute.

Dualism can follow the science of intelligence very well and still let things count as beings of their own; to this end it can take the science of nature as just such a system of the own being of things; each [science] would count for it as much as it likes; they have peaceful room side by side.
But in this way the essence of both sciences, to be sciences of the absolute, would be overlooked, for the absolute is no side-by-sideness.
zh: 另一个立场——本来要靠它来扬弃两门科学中矛盾的东西——则是这样一种立场：它不让其中一门或另一门科学算作关于绝对者的科学。
二元论完全可以跟随智性的科学，同时仍旧让事物作为自有的本质而有效；为此它可以把自然科学当作这样一个关于事物自身本质的体系；每一门[科学]在它那里想算多少就算多少；它们和睦地并立，各有其位。
但这样一来，两门科学的本质——即它们是关于绝对者的科学——就被忽略了，因为绝对者不是并列。

en: Or there is still another standpoint on which the one or the other science would not count as a science of the absolute, namely the one on which the principle of the one would be sublated as posited in the absolute, or the absolute as posited in the appearance of this principle.

The most remarkable standpoint in this respect is that of what is usually called transcendental idealism; it was asserted that this science of the subjective subject-object is itself one of the integrating sciences of philosophy, but also only the one.
It has been pointed out [what is] the one-sidedness of this science when it asserts itself as the science ϰατ' ἐξοχήν, and the shape which nature has from it.
Here there comes into consideration as well the form which the science of nature receives when it is built up from this standpoint.
zh: 或者还有一种立场，在其中一门或另一门科学不算作关于绝对者的科学，那就是这样一种立场：一方的原则被设定在绝对者之中、或者绝对者被设定在这一原则的现象之中，因而被扬弃了。
在这方面最值得注意的立场，就是通常所谓的先验观念论的立场；有人断言，这门关于主观的主体—客体的科学本身就是哲学中诸门整合性科学之一，但也只是其中之一。
这门科学的片面性——当它把自己主张为 ϰατ' ἐξοχήν 的科学时——以及自然界从它出发所具有的形态，都已经被指出来了。
这里还要考察的是，自然科学若从这一立场出发被建立起来，会得到怎样的形态。

en: Kant acknowledges a nature in that he posits the object as something (through the understanding) undetermined, and presents nature as a subject-object in that he regards the product of nature as a natural end, purposive without the concept of an end, necessary without mechanism, concept and being identical.

At the same time, however, this view of nature is to count only teleologically, that is, only as a maxim of our restricted, discursively thinking, human understanding, in whose general concepts the particular appearances of nature are said not to be contained; through this human way of considering things nothing is to be said about the reality of nature; the way of considering things therefore remains something thoroughly subjective, and nature a purely objective something, a merely thought something.

The synthesis of nature as determined and at the same time undetermined by the understanding in an intuitive understanding is indeed to remain a mere idea; it is indeed to be impossible for us human beings that explanation on the path of mechanism should meet with purposiveness.

These most subordinate and irrational critical views, even though they set human and absolute reason absolutely in opposition to each other, nevertheless rise to the idea of an intuitive understanding, that is, of reason; it is nevertheless not to be impossible in itself, that is, in reason, that natural mechanism and natural purposiveness should meet.

But Kant has not let fall the distinction between something possible in itself and something real, nor has he raised the necessary highest idea of an intuitive understanding to reality, and for that reason, in his science of nature, insight into the possibility of the fundamental forces is, on the one hand, altogether an impossibility for him, while on the other hand such a science of nature, for which nature is a matter, that is, something absolutely opposed, something not determining itself, can construct only a mechanics.

With the poverty of attractive and repulsive forces48) it has already made matter too rich; for force is an inner that produces an outer, a self-positing = I, and such a thing, from the purely idealist standpoint, cannot pertain to matter.
He conceives matter merely as the objective, the [element] opposed to the I; those forces are for him not only superfluous but either purely ideal, and then they are no forces, or transcendent.

For him there remains no dynamical but only a mathematical construction of the appearances.49) The carrying-through of the appearances, which must be given, through the categories can indeed yield various correct concepts, but no necessity for the appearances, and the chain of necessity is the formal element of what is scientific in the construction.
The concepts remain something accidental to nature, just as nature remains something accidental to the concepts.

Syntheses correctly constructed through categories would therefore not necessarily have their proofs in nature itself; nature can offer only manifold plays, which could count as accidental schemata for laws of the understanding — examples whose peculiar and living [character] would precisely to that extent fall away, in that only the determinations of reflection are cognized in them.
Conversely, the categories are only meagre schemata of nature.50)
zh: 康德承认有一种自然界，因为他把客体设定为（通过知性）未被规定的东西，并且把自然界描述为主体—客体，因为他把自然产物看作自然目的：合目的却没有目的概念，必然却没有机械作用，概念与存在同一。
但同时，这种对自然界的看法应当只是目的论地有效，也就是说，只作为我们受限制的、作推论式思维的人类知性的一条准则而有效，而自然界那些特殊的现象据说并不包含在这种知性的普遍概念里；通过这种人类的考察方式，据说关于自然界的实在性什么也没有说出；于是这种考察方式始终完全是主观的东西，而自然界是纯粹客观的东西，是单纯被思考的东西。
通过知性被规定、同时又不被规定的自然界在一个感性的知性中的综合，固然应当始终只是一个观念；对我们人来说，固然应当不可能让机械作用这条路上的解释与合目的性相合。
这些极其低级、不合乎理性的批判见解，尽管把人的理性和绝对理性绝对地互相对立起来，却毕竟还是上升到一种感性的知性、也就是理性的观念；自在说来，也就是说在理性中，自然机械作用和自然合目的性毕竟应当不是不可能相合。
但康德没有放弃自在可能的东西与实在的东西之间的区别，也没有把感性的知性这一必然的最高观念提升为实在性，因此在康德关于自然界的科学里，一方面，对基本力之可能性的洞见根本是不可能的，另一方面，这样一门关于自然界的科学——对它来说自然界是物质，即绝对对立的东西、自己不规定自己的东西——只能建构出一种力学。
这样一门科学凭吸引力和排斥力48)这种贫乏，已经把物质弄得太丰富了；因为力是一种内在的东西，它产生出外在的东西，是一种自我设定 = 我，而这样东西从纯粹观念论的立场看不可能属于物质。
康德只把物质以概念把握为客观的东西，即与我对立的东西；那些力在他看来不只是多余的，而且要么纯粹是观念的，那样它们就不是力，要么是超验的。
对他来说，剩下的不是对现象的动力学建构，而只是一种数学的建构。49)让那些必须被给予的现象通过范畴而得到贯彻，固然能给出各式各样正确的概念，但对现象来说给不出任何必然性，而必然性的链条才是建构中科学性的形式的东西。
概念始终是对自然界而言偶然的东西，正如自然界是对概念而言偶然的东西。
通过范畴正确建构起来的综合，因此不必然在自然界本身中有自己的例证；自然界所能提供的只是杂多的游戏，它们可以作为知性规律的偶然图型而有效，——这些例子，其特有的东西和活的东西恰恰会随之消失，因为其中被认识到的只是反思规定。
反过来说，范畴只是自然界的贫乏图型。50)

en: If nature is only matter and not subject-object, then no such scientific construction of nature remains possible, for which the knowing and the known must be one.

A reason that has made itself into reflection through absolute opposition to the object can, a priori and only through deduction, say more of nature than its general character of matter; this general character remains lying at the basis, while the manifold further determinations are posited for and through reflection.

Such a deduction has the appearance of an a priori from the fact that it posits the product of reflection, the concept, as something objective; because it posits nothing further, it admittedly remains immanent.
Such a deduction is in its essence the same as that view which recognizes in nature only external purposiveness.

The difference is only that the former proceeds more systematically from a determinate point, for example the body of the rational being; in both, nature is something absolutely determined by the concept - something foreign to it.

The teleological view, which recognizes nature as determined only according to external ends, has an advantage with respect to completeness, since it takes up the manifoldness of nature as it is empirically given.

The deduction of nature, by contrast, which starts from a determinate point and, because of its incompleteness, postulates something further - in which this deducing consists -, is immediately satisfied with what is postulated, which is immediately supposed to accomplish as much as the concept demands.

Whether an actual object of nature is able to accomplish what is demanded on its own does not concern it, and it can find this out only through experience; if the immediately postulated object does not prove sufficient in nature, then another is deduced, and so on, until the end finds itself fulfilled.

The order of these deduced objects depends on the determinate ends from which the deduction starts; and only insofar as they have a relation with respect to this end do they have coherence among themselves.

But properly they are capable of no inner coherence; for if the object that was immediately deduced is found in experience to be insufficient for the concept that is to be fulfilled, then through such a single object, because it is externally infinitely determinable, the dispersal into infinity is opened up - a dispersal that would perhaps be avoided only if the deduction turned its manifold points into a circle, but in whose inner centre it is not capable of placing itself, because it is in the external from the very beginning.
For the concept the object, for the object the concept, is something external.
zh: 如果自然只是物质，而不是主体—客体，那么就不可能有对自然的这样一种科学建构，在这种建构里，认识者和被认识者必须是同一个。
一种理性通过同客体的绝对对立而把自己变成了反思，它能够先验地、并且只靠演绎，就自然说出比自然的物质这一普遍性格更多的东西；这个普遍性格始终作为基础留在那里，而那些杂多的进一步规定则是为反思、并通过反思而被设定的。
这样一种演绎之所以带有先验性的假象，是因为它把反思的产物、即概念，设定为一种客观的东西；由于它不再设定别的东西，它当然始终是内在的。
这样一种演绎在本质上与那种在自然中只承认外在合目的性的看法是同一个东西。
差别只在于，前一种看法更系统地从某一个确定的点出发，例如从理性存在者的身体出发；在两者那里，自然都是被概念——一个对自然来说陌生的东西——绝对地规定的东西。
目的论的观点只承认自然是按外在目的被规定的，就完整性而言它有一个优点，因为它把自然在经验中被给予的那种杂多接纳了进来。
与此相反，自然的演绎从一个确定的点出发，并且由于这个点的不完整而还要求更多的东西——这种演绎就在于这一点——，它对于所要求的东西直接感到满足，而所要求的东西应当直接做到概念所要求的一切。
一个现实的自然客体是否单靠自己就能做到所要求的东西，这不关它的事，它只能通过经验发现这一点；如果在自然中那个直接被要求的客体显得不够用，那就演绎出另一个，如此等等，直到目的得到满足为止。
这些被演绎出来的客体的秩序，取决于演绎所从出发的那些确定的目的；而只有当它们就这个目的而言有一种关系时，它们彼此之间才有联系。
但严格说来，它们根本不能有什么内在的联系；因为如果那个直接被演绎出来的客体在经验中被发现不足以满足应当得到实现的概念，那么通过这样一个唯一的客体，由于它在外在方面是无限可规定的，散入无限就被打开了——这种分散也许只有靠演绎把它那些杂多的点转成一个圆圈才能避免，但演绎却没有能力把自己置入这个圆圈的内部中心，因为它从一开始就在外在之中。
对概念来说客体是外在的，对客体来说概念是外在的。

en: Thus neither of the two sciences can constitute itself as the only one, neither can sublate the other.

Thereby the absolute would be posited only in one form of its existence, and just as it posits itself in the form of existence, it must posit itself in a duality of form; for appearing and self-diremption are one.
zh: 所以两门科学中没有一门能把自己建立为唯一的科学，也没有一门能扬弃另一门。
这样一来，绝对者就只被设定在它存在的一种形式中；而正如它在存在的形式中设定自己，它也必然在形式的二重性中设定自己；因为显现和自我分裂是一回事。

en: Because of the inner identity of both sciences - since both present the absolute as it gives birth to itself out of the lower potencies of a form of appearance to totality in this form -, each science is, in its coherence and its sequence of stages, equal to the other.

The one is a confirmation of the other; as an older philosopher spoke of this roughly as follows: the order and connection of ideas (of the subjective) is the same as the connection and order of things51) (of the objective).

Everything is only in a totality; the objective totality and the subjective totality, the system of nature and the system of intelligence, is one and the very same; to a subjective determinacy there corresponds the very same objective determinacy.
zh: 由于两门科学的内在同一性——因为两者都陈述绝对者如何从一种显现形式的较低级次在这形式中把自己生成为总体性——，每一门科学按其联系和其阶段次序都与另一门相同。
一门是另一门的印证；正如一位较早的哲学家大致这样说过：观念（主观的东西）的秩序和联系，与事物51)（客观的东西）的联系和秩序是同一个。
一切都在一个总体性中；客观的总体性和主观的总体性、自然的体系和智性的体系，是同一个东西；与一种主观的规定性相对应的正是同一种客观的规定性。

en: As sciences they are objective totalities and proceed from something limited to something limited.

But every limited thing is itself in the absolute, hence inwardly something unlimited; it loses its external limitation through being posited in systematic coherence in the objective totality; in this it has truth even as a limited thing, and the knowing of it is the determination of its place.
To Jacobi's expression that the systems are an organized non-knowing52), it need only be added that the non-knowing - the cognition of individuals - becomes a knowing through being organized.
zh: 作为科学，它们是客观的总体性，并且从受限的东西走向受限的东西。
但每一个受限的东西本身就在绝对者之中，所以内在地是一个不受限的东西；它之所以失去自己外在的限制，是因为它在系统的联系中被设定在客观的总体性之中；在这种总体性里，它即使作为一个受限的东西也有真理，而对它的知就是规定它的位置。
对于雅可比说体系是一种被组织起来的非知识52)这一说法，只需补充一点：这种非知识——个别者的认识——由于被组织起来，就成为一种知识。

en: Besides the external equality, insofar as these sciences stand apart, their principles at the same time necessarily immediately interpenetrate each other.

If the principle of the one is the subjective subject-object, and of the other the objective subject-object, then in the system of subjectivity there is at the same time the objective, in the system of objectivity at the same time the subjective - nature being an immanent ideality just as much as intelligence is an immanent reality.

Both poles, of cognition and of being, are in each, so both also have the point of indifference within themselves; only in the one system the pole of the ideal, in the other the pole of the real, predominates.

The former does not in nature reach the point of absolute abstraction, which posits itself against infinite expansion as a point in itself, as the ideal constructs itself in reason; the latter does not in intelligence reach the involution53) of the infinite, which in this contraction posits itself infinitely outside itself, as the real constructs itself in matter.
Every system is a system of freedom and of necessity at the same time.

Freedom and necessity are ideal factors, hence not in real opposition; the absolute can therefore posit itself as absolute in neither of the two forms, and the sciences of philosophy cannot be, the one a system of freedom, the other a system of necessity.
Such a separated freedom would be a formal freedom, just as a separated necessity is a formal necessity.

Freedom is the character of the absolute when it is posited as something inner, which, insofar as it posits itself in a limited form, in determinate points of the objective totality, remains what it is, something not limited, when it is thus considered in opposition to its being, that is, as something inner, consequently with the possibility of leaving it and passing over into another appearance.

Necessity is the character of the absolute insofar as it is considered as something external, as an objective totality, hence as a being-outside-one-another, whose parts, however, have no being except in the whole of objectivity.
Because intelligence as well as nature, through being posited in the absolute, have a real opposition, the ideal factors of freedom and necessity belong to each of them.

But the semblance of freedom, arbitrariness, that is, a freedom in which there would be abstraction entirely from necessity or from freedom as a totality - which can only happen insofar as freedom is already posited within a single sphere -, as well as the chance corresponding to arbitrariness for necessity, with which individual parts are posited as if they were not in the objective totality and through it alone, but for themselves - arbitrariness and chance, which have room only on subordinate standpoints, are banished from the concept of the sciences of the absolute.
By contrast, necessity belongs to intelligence as it does to nature.
For since intelligence is posited in the absolute, the form of being likewise belongs to it; it must dirempt itself and appear; it is a completed organization of cognition and intuition.

Each of its shapes is conditioned by opposed ones, and if the abstract identity of the shapes is isolated as freedom from the shapes themselves, it is only an ideal pole of the point of indifference of intelligence, which has an objective totality as the other immanent pole.

Nature, by contrast, has freedom, for it is not a resting being but at the same time a becoming - a being that is not dirempted and synthesized from outside, but separates and unites itself within itself and in none of its shapes posits itself as something merely limited, but freely as the whole.

Its unconscious development is a reflection of the living force, which dirempts itself endlessly but in every limited shape posits itself and is identical; and in this respect no shape of nature is limited, but free.
zh: 除了这种外在的相同——就这两门科学各自分立而言——之外，它们的原则同时也必然直接相互渗透。
如果一门科学的原则是主观的主体—客体，另一门的是客观的主体—客体，那么在主观性的体系里同时也有客观的东西，在客观性的体系里同时也有主观的东西——自然是一种内在的观念性，正如智性是一种内在的实在性。
认识和存在的两个极都在每一门科学里，因此两者自身中也都有无差别点；只不过在一个体系里占优势的是观念物的极，在另一个体系里是实在物的极。
前者在自然中达不到绝对抽象这一点，这种抽象针对无限的扩展而把自己设定为自身中的点，就像观念物在理性中建构自己那样；后者在智性中达不到无限者的卷入53)，这种无限者在收缩中无限地把自己设定到自身之外，就像实在物在物质中建构自己那样。
每个体系都同时是自由的体系和必然性的体系。
自由和必然性是观念的要素，所以并不处于实在的对立之中；因此绝对者不能在这两种形式的任何一种中把自己设定为绝对者，而哲学的各门科学也不能一门是自由的体系、另一门是必然性的体系。
这样一种被分离开的自由会是一种形式的自由，正如一种被分离开的必然性是一种形式的必然性。
自由是绝对者的性格，当绝对者被设定为一种内在的东西时：这种内在的东西在把自己设定到一种受限的形式、设定到客观总体性的某些确定之点时，仍然保持它之所是，即一个不受限的东西；也就是说，当它被放在与自己存在的对立中、即被当作内在的东西来考察时，就带有离开自己的存在、过渡到另一种显现的可能性。
必然性是绝对者的性格，就绝对者被当作一种外在的东西、当作一种客观的总体性、也就是当作一种相互外在来考察而言，它的各个部分除了在客观性的整体中之外并没有存在。
由于智性以及自然都因为被设定在绝对者之中而有一种实在的对立，自由和必然性这两个观念的要素就属于它们中的每一个。
但是自由的假象，即任意——也就是一种完全从必然性、或从作为总体性的自由中抽象出来的自由，而这只有在自由已经被设定在一个单个领域之内时才可能发生——，以及同任意之于必然性相对应的偶然，即个别部分被设定得仿佛它们不是在客观的总体性中、不是仅仅通过这总体性，而是自为地存在——任意和偶然只在较低级的立场上才有立足之地，它们被逐出了关于绝对者的各门科学的概念。
相反，必然性属于智性，正如它属于自然。
因为智性既然被设定在绝对者之中，存在的形式也就同样属于它；它必须分裂自己并显现出来；它是认识和直观的一种完成了的组织。
它的每一种形态都由与之对立的形态所制约；而如果诸形态的抽象同一性被当作对诸形态本身的自由而孤立起来，那么它就只是智性的无差别点的一个观念的极，这个无差别点以客观的总体性作为另一个内在的极。
与此相反，自然拥有自由，因为它不是一种静止的存在，而同时是一种生成——一种不是从外面被分裂和被综合，而是在自身中自己分裂、自己统一的存在，并且它在自己的任何一种形态中都不把自己设定为一个仅仅受限的东西，而是自由地设定为整体。
它那无意识的发展是一种活的力的反思，这种力无限地分裂自己，但在每一种受限的形态中都设定自己并且是同一的；就此而言，自然的任何一种形态都不是受限的，而是自由的。

en: If therefore the science of nature in general is the theoretical part, the science of intelligence the practical part of philosophy, then at the same time each again has for itself its own theoretical and practical part.

As in the system of nature the identity in the potency of light, of heavy matter, is not in itself but as potency something foreign, which dirempts this identity and unites it into cohesion and produces a system of inorganic nature, so for the intelligence producing itself in objective intuitions the identity in the potency of self-positing is something not present, — the identity does not cognize itself in intuition; both are a producing of the identity that does not reflect on its acting, thus the object of a theoretical part.

But just as, on the other hand, in the will the intelligence cognizes itself and posits itself as itself into objectivity, annihilates its unconsciously produced intuitions, so nature becomes practical in organic nature, in that the light steps forth to its product and becomes an inner.

If in inorganic nature it posits the point of contraction outwardly into crystallization as an external ideality, so in organic nature the light forms itself as an inner into the contraction of the brain, already in the plant as the flower, in which the inner principle of light disperses itself in colours and quickly withers away in them; but in it, as more firmly in the animal, it posits itself through the polarity of the sexes subjectively and objectively at once; the individual seeks and finds itself in another.

More intensively does the light remain in the inner in the animal, in which, as a more or less changeable voice, it posits its individuality as something subjective in universal communication, [as] cognizing and acknowledging itself.
In that natural science presents the identity as it reconstructs the moments of inorganic nature from within, it has within itself a practical part.

The reconstructed, practical magnetism is the sublation of gravity expanding outwardly into poles, its recontraction into the point of indifference of the brain, and its transposition of the two poles inward, as two points of indifference, as nature also sets them up in the elliptical orbits of the planets; electricity reconstructed from within posits the sexual difference of the organizations, each of which produces the difference through itself, posits itself ideally on account of its lack, finds itself objectively in another, and must give itself identity through flowing together with it.

Nature, insofar as it becomes practical through the chemical process, has laid back into itself as an inner the third, the mediating of the different, which as tone, an inner self-producing ringing, is like the third body of the inorganic process something without potency and passes away, extinguishes the absolute substantiality of the different beings and brings them to the indifference of mutual self-acknowledgement, of an ideal positing that does not again, like the sexual relation, die away in a real identity.
zh: 因此，如果自然科学总体上是哲学的理论部分、智性的科学是哲学的实践部分，那么两者同时又各自有一个自己的理论部分和实践部分。
正如在自然的体系中，光明这一级次上的同一性、即重物质，并不是自在的，而是作为级次是一个异己的东西，它把这种同一性分裂开来、又使它联合为凝聚，并产生出一个无机自然的体系；同样，对于在客观直观中生产自身的智性来说，自我设定这一级次上的同一性是一个并不存在的东西——同一性在直观中并不认识自身；两者都是一种不反思自身行动的对同一性的生产，因而是理论部分的对象。
但另一方面，正如在意志中智性认识自身、并把自己作为自身置入客观性之中，消灭掉它无意识地生产出来的直观，同样，自然在有机自然中成为实践的，因为光明走向自己的产物并成为一个内在的东西。
如果它在无机自然中把收缩点向外设定为结晶、作为一种外在的观念性，那么光明在有机自然中就把自己作为内在的东西形成为大脑的收缩，在植物中已经形成为花，内在的光原则在花中分散为颜色、又在这些颜色中迅速枯萎；但在植物中，正如在动物中更牢固地，光明通过两性的极性把自己同时主观地和客观地设定起来；个体在另一个个体中寻找并找到自身。
光明在动物中更强烈地留在内在之中；在动物那里，它作为或多或少可变的声音，在普遍的传达中把自己的个体性设定为一种主观的东西，[作为]认识自身并承认自身的东西。
由于自然科学把同一性描述出来，即描述它如何从内部重新建构无机自然的诸环节，所以它在自身中有一个实践的部分。
被重新建构起来的、实践的磁力，是对向外扩展为两极的重力的扬弃，是重力向大脑的无差别点的重新收缩，也是把两个极移向内部、作为两个无差别点，正如自然在行星的椭圆轨道上也把它们设定起来一样；从内部重新建构起来的电，设定诸组织的性别差别，这些组织每一个都通过自身产生出差别，由于自己的匮乏而把自身观念地设定起来，在另一个组织中客观地找到自身，并且必须通过与它合流而把同一性给予自己。
自然，就它通过化学过程成为实践的而言，已经把第三个东西、即把有差别者中介起来的东西，作为一个内在的东西放回到自身之中，这个东西作为声音、即一种内在的自己生产自身的鸣响，和无机过程的第三个物体一样是没有级次的并且消逝，它抹去那些有差别的存在者的绝对实体性，并把它们带到相互自我承认的无差别，带到一种观念的设定，这种设定不再像性别关系那样在一种实在的同一性中死去。

en: So far we have opposed the two sciences to one another in their inner identity; in the one the absolute is something subjective in the form of cognition, in the other something objective in the form of being.

Being and cognition thereby become ideal factors or forms in that they are opposed to one another; in both sciences both are present, but in the one cognition is the matter and being the form, in the other being is the matter and cognition the form.

Because the absolute is the same in both, and the sciences represent not merely the opposed as forms but, insofar as the subject-object posits itself in them, the subject-object, so the sciences themselves are not in ideal but in real opposition, and therefore they must at the same time be considered in a continuity, as one coherent science.

Insofar as they are opposed to one another, they are indeed inwardly enclosed in themselves and totalities, but at the same time only relative ones, and as such they strive toward the point of indifference; as identity and as relative totality it lies everywhere within themselves, as absolute totality outside them.

But insofar as both sciences of the absolute and their opposition are a real one, they hang together as poles of indifference in this indifference itself; they themselves are the lines that link the pole with the centre.
But this centre is itself a doubled one, at one time identity, at the other totality, and insofar both sciences appear as the progress of the development or self-construction of identity to totality.

The point of indifference toward which the two sciences, insofar as they are opposed when considered from the side of their ideal factors, strive, is the whole, represented as a self-construction of the absolute, the last and highest of them.

The middle, the point of transition from the identity constructing itself as nature to its construction as intelligence, is the becoming-inner of the light of nature, — the, as Schelling says54), striking flash of the ideal into the real and its self-constitution as point.

This point, as reason the turning point of both sciences, is the highest peak of the pyramid of nature, its last product, at which nature, completing itself, arrives; but as point it must likewise expand into a nature.

If the science has placed itself in it as centre and from it divided itself into two parts, and assigns to the one side unconscious production, to the other conscious production, then it knows at the same time that the intelligence, as a real factor, at the same time carries over with itself the whole self-construction of nature on the other side and has in itself what precedes it or stands at its side, as also that in nature, as a real factor, what stands opposed to it in science is likewise immanent.

And with this all ideality of the factors and their one-sided form is sublated; this is the single higher standpoint on which both sciences are lost in one another, in that their separation is acknowledged only as something scientific and the ideality of the factors only as something posited for this purpose.

This view is immediately only negative, only the sublation of the separation of both sciences and of the forms in which the absolute has posited itself, not a real synthesis, not the absolute point of indifference in which these forms are annihilated by the fact that, united, both persist.

The original identity, which expanded its unconscious contraction — subjectively that of feeling, objectively that of matter — into the endlessly organized side-by-side and succession of space and time, into objective totality, and opposed to this expansion the contraction constituting itself through the annihilation of that expansion, into the self-cognizing point of (subjective) reason, the subjective totality, must unite both into the intuition of the absolute becoming objective to itself in completed totality — into the intuition of the eternal incarnation of God, of the begetting of the Word from the beginning.
zh: 迄今为止，我们在两者的内在同一性上把两门科学彼此对立起来；在其中的一门里，绝对者是以认识的形式出现的主观的东西，在另一门里，是以存在的形式出现的客观的东西。
存在和认识由于互相对立而成为观念的因素或形式；在两门科学中两者都在，但在其中一门里认识是质料、存在是形式，在另一门里存在是质料、认识是形式。
因为绝对者在两门科学中是同一个，而各门科学所描述的不仅是作为形式的对立面，而且——就主体—客体在它们之中设定自身而言——是主体—客体，所以各门科学本身并不处于观念的对立中，而是处于实在的对立中，因此它们同时必须在一种连续性中、作为一门前后相贯的科学来考察。
就它们互相对立而言，它们固然是内在地自封闭的、是总体性，但同时只是相对的总体性，并且作为这样的总体性趋向无差别点；作为同一性和相对的总体性，这个无差别点处处都在它们自身之内，作为绝对的总体性则在它们之外。
但就两门关于绝对者的科学及其对立是实在的而言，它们作为无差别的两极就在这个无差别本身中相互联属；它们本身就是把极与中心点连接起来的线。
但这个中心点本身是双重的，一则是同一性，另一则是总体性，就此而言，两门科学显得是同一性向总体性的发展或自我建构的进程。
两门科学就其观念的因素方面来看是对立的，它们所趋向的那个无差别点就是整体——被表象为绝对者的一种自我建构——，是它们之中最后和最高的东西。
中间者，即从把自身建构为自然的同一性向它作为智性的建构的过渡点，就是自然之光的变为内在，——即如谢林所说54) 那样闪入实在物之中的观念物的闪电，以及它作为点而自我构成。
这个点，作为理性是两门科学的转折点，是自然之金字塔的最高峰，是自然最后的产品，自然在自我完成时到达这个产品；但作为点，它同样必须扩展为一种自然。
如果科学已把自己置入这个点作为中心点、并从它把自己分为两个部分，把无意识的生产分给一边、把有意识的生产分给另一边，那么它同时知道：智性作为一个实在的因素，同时把另一边的整个自然之自我建构一起带过来，并把先行于它的东西或与它并列的东西包含在自身之中；同样，在自然作为一个实在的因素那里，在科学中与它相对立的东西也同样是内在的。
而这样一来，诸因素的全部观念性及其片面的形式就被扬弃了；这是唯一更高的立足点，在这个立足点上两门科学互相消融于对方之中，因为它们的分离只被承认为一种科学性的东西，诸因素的观念性也只被承认为为了这一目的而设定起来的东西。
这种看法直接地只是否定的，只是对两门科学的分离以及绝对者已把自身置入其中的那些形式的扬弃，而不是一种实在的综合，也不是那个绝对的无差别点——在那个无差别点里，这些形式之所以被消灭，正是因为它们联合起来、两者都持存。
原初的同一性，它把自己无意识的收缩——主观上是感觉的收缩，客观上是物质的收缩——扩展为空间和时间中无限地组织起来的并列与相继、扩展为客观的总体性，并给这种扩展对立地设置那种通过消灭扩展而把自己建构起来的收缩，即向(主观)理性之自我认识的点、向主观总体性的收缩，这个原初的同一性必须把两者联合起来，带入对在完成的总体性中自身成为客观的绝对者的直观——带入对上帝之永恒道成肉身、对从开端生育圣言的直观。

en: This intuition of the absolute forming itself or finding itself objectively can likewise again be considered in a polarity, insofar as of the factors of this equilibrium, on the one side consciousness, on the other the unconscious, is posited as predominant.

That intuition appears in art more concentrated into one point and bringing down consciousness, — either in art properly so called as work, which as objective is partly enduring, partly can be taken with the understanding as a dead external, a product of the individual, of genius, but belonging to humanity, — or in religion as a living movement, which as subjective, only filling moments, can be posited by the understanding as a merely inner thing, the product of a multitude, of a universal genius, but also belonging to every single individual.
In speculation that intuition appears more as consciousness, and what is spread out in consciousness as an activity of subjective reason, which sublates objectivity and the unconscious.

If to art in its true extent the absolute appears more in the form of absolute being, so it appears to speculation more as something self-producing in its infinite intuition; but while speculation indeed grasps it as a becoming, it posits at the same time the identity of becoming and being, and what appears to it as self-producing is at the same time posited as the original absolute being, which can only become insofar as it is.
In this way it knows how to take from itself the predominance that consciousness has in it, — a predominance that is in any case something unessential.
Both, art and speculation, are in their essence divine service, — both a living intuition of absolute life and thus a being-one with it.
zh: 这种对自我构形或在自身那里客观地找到自身的绝对者的直观，同样又可以放在一种极性中来考察，因为这种平衡的诸因素中，一边的意识、另一边的无意识，被设定为占优势的。
那种直观在艺术中显得更多地凝聚于一个点并使意识沉降，——或者在真正所谓的艺术中作为作品，这作品作为客观的东西一部分是持久的，一部分可以被知性当作一个死的外在物，它是个人、即天才的产物，却属于人类，——或者在宗教中作为一种活生生的运动，这种运动作为主观的东西、只充实诸环节，可以被知性设定为一个单纯内在的东西，它是一个群体、一种普遍天才性的产物，但也属于每一个个体。
在思辨中，那种直观更多地作为意识出现，而在意识中展开的东西则作为主观理性的行动出现，这种理性扬弃客观性和无意识的东西。
如果说在艺术中、在其真正的范围内，绝对者更多地以绝对存在的形式出现，那么它在思辨中则更多地作为在其无限直观中自我产生的东西出现；但思辨虽然把它理解为一种生成，却同时设定生成与存在的同一性，而那个对它来说显得是自我产生的东西，同时被设定为原初的绝对存在，这种存在只有在它存在时才能生成。
思辨以这种方式懂得自己去掉意识在它之中所具有的优势，——这种优势本来就只是一种非本质的东西。
两者，艺术和思辨，就其本质而言都是事奉上帝，——两者都是对绝对生命的活生生的直观，因而都是与它的一体。

en: Speculation and its knowledge is thus in the point of indifference, but not in and for itself in the true point of indifference; whether it is in it depends on whether it recognizes itself only as one side of it.

Transcendental philosophy is a science of the absolute, for the subject is itself subject-object and to that extent reason; if it posits itself as this subjective reason as the absolute, then it is a pure, i.e. formal reason, whose products, ideas, are absolutely opposed to a sensibility or nature and can serve appearances only as the rule of a unity foreign to them.

Insofar as the absolute is posited in the form of a subject, this science has an immanent limit; it raises itself to the science of the absolute and into the absolute point of indifference solely by knowing its limit and knowing how to sublate itself and that limit, and indeed scientifically.

For much was indeed formerly spoken of the boundary posts of human reason, and transcendental idealism too acknowledges incomprehensible bounds of self-consciousness, into which we are once and for all enclosed; but since the bounds are there passed off as boundary posts of reason, here as incomprehensible, the science recognizes its inability to sublate itself through itself, i.e. not through a salto mortale, or to abstract again from the subjective into which it has posited reason.
zh: 思辨及其知识因此就在无差别点中，但不是自在自为地在真正的无差别点中；它是否在无差别点中，取决于它是否只把自己认作无差别点的一个方面。
先验哲学是关于绝对者的一门科学，因为主体本身就是主体—客体，就此而言就是理性；如果先验哲学把自身作为这种主观理性设定为绝对者，那它就是一种纯粹的、即形式的理性，这种理性的产物、即观念，与一种感性或自然是绝对对立的，并且对现象来说只能充当一条规则，即一种与现象陌生的统一性。
由于绝对者被设定在主体的形式中，这门科学就有一条内在的界限；它唯有认识到自己的界限、并且懂得把自己和这条界限一并扬弃，而且是以科学的方式扬弃，才上升到关于绝对者的科学、上升到绝对的无差别点。
因为从前确实有很多人谈论人类理性的界桩，先验观念论也承认自我意识有不可理解的界限，我们终究被关在这些界限里面；但既然这些界限在那里被说成理性的界桩、在这里被说成不可理解的，这门科学就认识到自己没有能力通过自身、即不是通过一次 salto mortale，把自己扬弃，也没有能力从它把理性置入其中的那个主观的东西里重新抽象出来。

en: Because transcendental philosophy posits its subject as a subject-object and is herewith one side of the absolute point of indifference, the totality is indeed in it; the entire philosophy of nature itself falls as a knowing within its sphere, and the science of knowing, which would constitute only one part of transcendental philosophy, cannot be forbidden, any more than logic, to lay claim to the form that it gives to knowing and to the identity that is in knowing, or rather to isolate the form as consciousness and to construct the appearance for itself.

But this identity, separated from all the manifold of knowing, as pure self-consciousness, shows itself as a relative one in that it does not emerge from its being conditioned by an opposed in any of its forms.
zh: 因为先验哲学把它的主体设定为一个主体—客体，因此是绝对无差别点的一个方面，所以总体性确实就在它之中；整个自然哲学本身也作为一种知识落入它的领域之内，而关于知识的科学——它只会构成先验哲学的一个部分——不能被禁止，正如逻辑不能被禁止一样，去对它赋予知识的形式、对知识中存在的同一性提出要求，或者毋宁说，去把形式作为意识孤立起来，并自为地建构现象。
但这种同一性，在从知识的一切杂多中分离出来之后，作为纯粹自我意识，却显示为一种相对的同一性，因为它无论在自己的哪一种形式里都走不出自己受一个对立面制约的状态。

en: The absolute principle, the sole real ground and firm standpoint of philosophy, is in Fichte's philosophy as in Schelling's the intellectual intuition, - expressed for reflection: identity of subject and object.

In science it becomes the object of reflection; and therefore philosophical reflection is itself transcendental intuition, it makes itself into an object and is one with it; through this it is speculation.
Fichte's philosophy is therefore a genuine product of speculation.

Philosophical reflection is conditioned, or transcendental intuition comes into consciousness through free abstraction from all manifoldness of empirical consciousness, and to that extent it is something subjective.

If philosophical reflection in this respect makes itself into an object, then it makes something conditioned into the principle of its philosophy; in order to grasp transcendental intuition purely, it must abstract further from this subjective element, so that transcendental intuition is for it as the foundation of philosophy neither subjective nor objective, neither self-consciousness opposed to matter, nor matter opposed to self-consciousness, but absolute, neither subjective nor objective identity, pure transcendental intuition.
As object of reflection it becomes subject and object; these products of pure reflection philosophical reflection posits, in their abiding opposition, into the absolute.

The opposition of speculative reflection is no longer an object and a subject, but a subjective transcendental intuition and an objective transcendental intuition, the former I, the latter nature - both the highest appearances of the absolute, self-intuiting reason.

That these two opposed - they are now called I and nature, pure and empirical self-consciousness, cognition and being, self-positing and opposing, finitude and infinity - are at the same time posited in the absolute, in this antinomy ordinary reflection sees nothing but the contradiction, only reason in this absolute contradiction the truth, through which both are posited and both are annihilated, neither both, and both at once.
zh: 哲学的绝对原则、唯一的实在根据和牢固立足点，在费希特的哲学里和在谢林的哲学里一样，都是智性直观，——用反思的方式说出来就是：主体与客体的同一性。
在科学中，智性直观成为反思的对象；因此，哲学反思本身就是先验直观，它把自己变成对象，并与对象是同一的；由此它就是思辨。
费希特的哲学因此是思辨的真正产物。
哲学反思是有条件的，或者说，先验直观是通过从经验意识的一切杂多中自由抽象而进入意识的，就此而言它是一种主观的东西。
如果哲学反思就此把自己变成对象，那它就是把一种有条件的东西当成了自己哲学的原则；为了纯粹地把握先验直观，它还必须从这种主观的东西中抽象掉，使先验直观作为哲学的基础对它来说既不是主观的、也不是客观的，既不是与物质相对立的自我意识，也不是与自我意识相对立的物质，而是绝对的、既非主观也非客观的同一性，是纯粹的先验直观。
作为反思的对象，先验直观成为主体和客体；这些纯粹反思的产物，哲学反思把它们连同其持续不变的对立一并设定到绝对者之中。
思辨反思的对立不再是一个客体和一个主体，而是一种主观的先验直观和一种客观的先验直观，前者是我，后者是自然，——两者都是绝对的、自己直观自身的理性的最高现象。
这两个对立面——它们现在叫作我和自然、纯粹的和经验的自我意识、认识与存在、自我设定与对立设定、有限性与无限性——同时被设定在绝对者之中，面对这一二律背反，普通反思看到的只是矛盾，唯有理性在这一绝对矛盾中看到真理：通过这一矛盾，两者都被设定，两者都被消灭，既不是两者，又同时是两者。

25.zh: [论赖因霍尔德对哲学的看法]

en: It still remains to speak, partly of something about Reinhold's view of Fichte's and Schelling's philosophy, partly of his own.
zh: 还剩下一些话要说：一部分是关于赖因霍尔德对费希特哲学和谢林哲学的看法，一部分是关于他自己的看法。

en: As regards that view, Reinhold has, in the first place, overlooked the difference of the two as systems, and, in the second place, has not taken them as philosophies.
zh: 就那种看法来说，赖因霍尔德首先忽略了两者作为体系的差别，其次没有把它们当作哲学来对待。

en: Reinhold seems not to have suspected that for year and day a different philosophy has lain before the public than pure transcendental idealism; he sees, wonderfully enough, in philosophy as Schelling has set it up, nothing but a principle of the comprehensible of subjectivity, I-hood.55) Reinhold is capable of saying in one connection that Schelling has made the discovery that the absolute, insofar as it is not mere subjectivity, is and can be nothing further than mere objectivity or mere nature as such, and that the way to this is to posit the absolute in the absolute identity of intelligence and nature,56) - thus in one breath to present Schelling's principle as follows: a) the absolute, insofar as it is not mere subjectivity, is mere objectivity, thus not the identity of the two, and b) the absolute is the identity of the two.
Conversely, the principle of the identity of subject and object had to become the way to see that the absolute as identity is neither mere subjectivity nor mere objectivity.

Correctly, Reinhold afterwards presents the relation of the two sciences as being that both are only different views of one and the very same - not of a thing, to be sure, but of absolute sameness, of the All-one.

And precisely for this reason neither the principle of the one nor the principle of the other is mere subjectivity or mere objectivity, still less that in which both alone interpenetrate, pure I-hood, which, like nature, is swallowed up in the absolute point of indifference.
zh: 赖因霍尔德似乎没有料到，很久以来摆在公众面前的是另一种哲学，而不是纯粹的先验观念论；他奇怪地在谢林所建立起来的哲学里看到的，无非是主观性之可理解者的一条原则，即我性。55)赖因霍尔德竟能在同一段话里说，谢林作出了这样的发现：绝对者只要不是单纯的主观性，就无非是、也只能是单纯的客观性，或单纯的自然本身，而通向这一点的道路就是把绝对者设定在智性与自然的绝对同一性之中，56)，——于是一口气把谢林的原则说成这样：a) 绝对者只要不是单纯的主观性，就是单纯的客观性，因而并不是两者的同一性，而 b) 绝对者是两者的同一性。
反过来，主体与客体同一性的原则必定成为一条道路，以便看出绝对者作为同一性既不是单纯的主观性，也不是单纯的客观性。
随后赖因霍尔德正确地这样表述两门科学的关系：两者只是对同一个东西——当然不是对一个事物，而是对绝对的同者，对太一——的不同看法。
也正因如此，无论这一门的原则还是那一门的原则，都不是单纯的主观性或单纯的客观性，更不是两者唯一在其中相互渗透的那个东西，即纯粹的我性——它和自然一样，在绝对的无差别点中被吞没。

en: Whoever, Reinhold thinks, is taken not by system but by love and faith in truth, will easily convince himself that the error of this described solution lies in the manner of grasping the task, - but wherein the error of Reinhold's descriptions of what philosophy is according to Schelling lies, and how this manner of grasping it was possible, about that it is not so easy to find elucidation.
zh: 赖因霍尔德认为，谁若是由对真理的爱和信仰、而不是由体系所左右，就容易说服自己：上述解决方式的错误在于把握任务的方式，——但赖因霍尔德对那些按谢林来说是哲学的东西所作描述的错在哪里，这种把握方式又怎么可能，对此就不那么容易得到说明了。

en: It cannot help to refer to the introduction to transcendental idealism itself, in which its relation to the whole of philosophy and the concept of this whole of philosophy is set forth; for in his judgements of it Reinhold restricts himself to this introduction and sees the opposite in it of what is in it.

Just as little can attention be drawn to individual passages of it in which the true point of view is expressed most determinately; for the most determinate passages Reinhold himself cites in his first judgement of this system, - which contain that only in the one necessary foundational science of philosophy, in transcendental idealism, is the subjective the first,57) not, as in Reinhold the matter immediately inverts itself, the first of the whole of philosophy, nor, as purely subjective, even the principle of transcendental idealism, but as subjective subject-object.
zh: 指出先验观念论本身的导论也无济于事，因为在这篇导论里，先验观念论与哲学整体的关系以及哲学这一整体的概念已被提了出来；赖因霍尔德在对此书的评判中恰恰把自己限制在这篇导论上，并且从中看到的与其中实际有的正好相反。
同样也不能让人去注意这部著作中那些最确定地道出真正观点的个别段落；因为最确定的段落，赖因霍尔德本人在他对这一体系的第一次评判中就引用过，——它们所包含的是：只有在哲学的那一门必然的基础科学，即先验观念论里，主观的东西才是最初的东西，57)，而不是——像在赖因霍尔德那里事情立刻就被颠倒过来那样——整个哲学的最初东西，也不是作为纯粹主观的东西、哪怕只作为先验观念论的原则，而是作为主观的主体—客体。

en: For those who are capable of not hearing, from determinate expressions, the opposite of them, it is perhaps not superfluous, besides the introduction to the system of transcendental idealism itself and, in any case, the more recent pieces of the Journal for Speculative Physics, to draw attention already to the second piece of the first volume of the same, in which Schelling expresses himself thus [S. 84 f.]: "The philosophy of nature is a physical explanation of idealism; ... nature has from afar already made the disposition to this height, which it reaches in reason.

The philosopher overlooks this only because he takes up his object with the first act already in the highest potency, - as I as endowed with consciousness, and only the physicist gets behind this illusion ...

The idealist is right when he makes reason the self-creator of everything, ... he has for himself nature's own intention with man; but precisely because it is the intention of nature, ... that idealism itself becomes ... something explicable, and with that the theoretical reality of idealism collapses.
When men first learn to think purely theoretically, merely objectively, without any admixture of the subjective, then they will learn to understand this."
zh: 对于那些能从确定的说法里听不出其反面的人来说，除了《先验观念论体系》本身的导论以及《思辨物理学杂志》较新的几篇之外，不妨再提醒他们注意同一杂志第一卷第2篇，谢林在其中这样说[S. 84 f.]：“自然哲学是对观念论的一种物理学解释；……自然早已远远地为这一高度作了准备，这一高度它是在理性中才达到。
哲学家之所以忽略这一点，只是因为他从最初的行为起就把自己的对象当作已经处在最高级次上的东西来接受，——当作我，当作具有意识的东西，而只有物理学家才识破这一假象……
观念论者把理性说成一切东西的自我创造者，这是对的，……他把握到了自然在人身上所抱有的自身意图；但正因为这是自然的意图，……那种观念论本身也就……成了某种可解释的东西，而观念论的理论实在性也随之垮掉。
等到人们学会纯粹理论地、仅仅客观地、不掺入任何主观的东西去思维，他们就会学会理解这一点。”

en: If Reinhold locates the chief defect of previous philosophy in this, that thinking has hitherto been represented under the character of a merely subjective activity, and demands that the attempt be made to abstract from its subjectivity,58) then — as lies not only in what has been cited but in the principle of Schelling's whole system — the abstraction from the subjective of transcendental intuition is the formal basic character of this philosophy, — which more determinately [in the] Zeitschrift für spekulative Physik, II.

St. has come to be discussed, on the occasion of Eschenmayer's objections against the philosophy of nature, which are taken from grounds of transcendental idealism, in which the totality is posited only as an idea, a thought, i.e., something subjective.
zh: 如果赖因霍尔德把以往哲学的主要毛病放在这一点上，即人们至今把思维放在一种纯然主观活动的特征之下加以表象，并要求人们尝试从这种思维的主观性中抽象出来，58）那么——这一点不仅存在于前面所引的话里，而且存在于谢林整个体系的原则里——从先验直观的主观东西中抽象出来，就是这一哲学的形式上的基本特征，——它还更确切地在《思辨物理学杂志》第 II
Bd.，第 1
St. 得到了表达，那是在埃申迈尔针对自然哲学的责难之际，这些责难取自先验观念论的理由，在先验观念论里，总体性只被设定为一种观念、一个思想，也就是某种主观的东西。

en: As for Reinhold's view of the common side of both systems, that they are speculative philosophies, they necessarily appear to Reinhold's peculiar standpoint as peculiarities, and consequently not as philosophies.

If, according to Reinhold, the most essential business, theme and principle of philosophy is to ground the reality of cognition through analysis, i.e., through separating,59) then speculation, whose highest task is to sublate the separation in the identity of subject and object, of course has no significance at all, and the most essential side of a philosophical system, that of being speculation, cannot then come into consideration; nothing remains but a peculiar view and a stronger or weaker aberration of spirit.

Thus, e.g., materialism too appears to Reinhold only from the side of an aberration of spirit, which is said not to be native to Germany,60) and he recognizes in it nothing of the genuine philosophical need to sublate the diremption in the form of spirit and matter.

If the western locality of the culture out of which this system has emerged keeps it away from a country, then the question is whether this remoteness does not stem from an opposite one-sidedness of culture; and even if its scientific value were quite slight, at the same time it is not to be overlooked that, e.g., in the Système de la nature61) there speaks a spirit that has become at odds with its time and reproduces itself in science, and how the grief over the universal deception of its time, over the bottomless derangement of nature, over the infinite lie that called itself truth and right — how the grief over this, which blows through the whole, retains strength enough to construct for itself the absolute that has fled from the appearance of life, as truth, with a genuinely philosophical need and true speculation, in a science whose form appears in the local principle of the objective, just as German culture, by contrast, often nests in the form of the subjective — to which love and faith also belong — without speculation. — Because the analytic side, since it rests on absolute opposition, must overlook in a philosophy precisely its philosophical side, the side that aims at absolute union, it seems to it most strange of all that Schelling, as Reinhold puts it, has introduced the connection of the finite and the infinite into philosophy, — as if philosophizing were something other than positing the finite in the infinite; — in other words: it seems to it most strange that philosophizing is to be introduced into philosophy.
zh: 至于赖因霍尔德对两个体系共同的那一面的看法，即它们都是思辨哲学，那么从赖因霍尔德那个独特的立场来看，它们就必然显得是一些特殊的东西，因而并不是哲学。
如果按赖因霍尔德所说，哲学最本质的事务、主题和原则就是通过分析、也就是通过分离来论证认识的实在性，59）那么思辨——它的最高任务是在主体与客体的同一性中扬弃分离——当然就完全没有任何意义，而一个哲学体系最本质的一面，即它是思辨，这时也就无从谈起；剩下的只是一个独特的看法和或强或弱的精神迷误。
例如，在赖因霍尔德看来，唯物论也只是从精神迷误这一面出现的，而这种迷误据说在德意志并不本土，60）他在其中根本看不出那种真正的哲学需要，即扬弃以精神与物质的形式出现的分裂。

如果这个体系由之产生的教养的西方地域把它挡在一个国家之外，那么问题就在于，这种疏远是不是来自教养的一种相反的单面性；而即便它的科学价值微不足道，同时也不可否认：例如在 Système de la nature（《自然的体系》）61）里，有一种与自己的时代闹翻、并在科学中自我再生产的精神在说话，而且，对它的时代的普遍欺骗、对自然的那种没有根基的错乱、对那种自称真理与权利的无限谎言的悲愤——这种贯穿整体的悲愤——还留有足够的力量，让那个从生命现象中逃走了的绝对者，带着真正的哲学需要和真正的思辨，在一种科学中为自己建构为真理，这种科学的形式显现在客观东西这一地方性原则里；而德意志教养相反，常常没有思辨就安顿在主观东西的形式里——爱与信仰也属于这种形式。——因为分析的一面既然建立在绝对对立之上，就必然在一个哲学那里恰恰看漏它哲学的一面，即走向绝对统一的那一面，所以它觉得最最奇怪的是：用赖因霍尔德的话说，谢林把有限与无限的结合引进了哲学，——就好像哲学活动是某种别的东西，而不是把有限设定到无限中去；——换句话说：它觉得最奇怪的是，应当把哲学活动引进哲学里去。

en: Likewise, in the Fichtean and Schellingian system Reinhold overlooks not only the speculative, philosophical side in general, but he holds it to be an important discovery and revelation when the principles of this philosophy transform themselves for him into the most utterly particular, and the most universal, the identity of subject and object, transforms itself for him into the most particular, namely the own, individual individuality of Messrs. Fichte and Schelling.62)
If Reinhold thus falls from the mountain of his limited principle and his peculiar view down into the abyss of the limited view of these systems, this is understandable and necessary.

But the turn is contingent and spiteful when Reinhold will provisionally, in the Teutscher Merkur,63) and more at length in the next issue of the Beiträge,64) explain the particularity of these systems from immorality, and indeed in such a way that immorality would have received in these systems the form of a principle and of philosophy.
One may call and abuse such a turn a wretchedness, a stopgap of embitterment, etc., as one likes; for such stuff is fair game.

To be sure, a philosophy does emerge out of its age and, if one wants to grasp the age's tornness as an immorality, out of immorality, — but in order, against the derangement of the age, to restore man out of himself and to preserve the totality that the time has torn apart.
zh: 同样，在费希特和谢林的体系里，赖因霍尔德不仅看漏了思辨的、哲学的一面本身，而且他还把下面这件事当成一项重要发现和启示：这一哲学的原则在他那里变成了最最个别的东西，而那最普遍的东西，即主体与客体的同一性，在他那里变成了最特殊的东西，也就是费希特先生和谢林先生各自个人的个别性。62）
如果赖因霍尔德就这样从他那个有限原则和他那个独特看法的山上，跌进这些体系的有限看法的深渊，那么这是可以理解、也是必然的。
但下面这个转折却是偶然的、恶意的：赖因霍尔德将暂时在《德意志信使》（Teutscher Merkur）63）上、并在下一期《论文集》64）上更详细地把这些体系的特殊性解释为出自不道德，而且是这样：不道德在这些体系里竟然取得了原则和哲学的形式。
人们可以随自己的意，把这样一个转折叫作并骂作可鄙、愤懑时的应急办法等等；因为这类东西是任人宰割的。
当然，一种哲学是从它的时代里产生出来的，并且如果人们愿意把时代的撕裂以概念把握为一种不道德，那它就是从这种不道德中产生出来的，——但这是为了针对时代的错乱，从人自身出发把人重新建立起来，并保住被时代撕裂了的总体性。

en: As for Reinhold's own philosophy, he gives a public history of it, namely that in the course of his philosophical metempsychosis he first migrated into the Kantian one, after laying that one aside into the Fichtean one, from this into the Jacobian one, and, since he has also left that one, has moved into Bardili's logic.

After he, according to S. 163 of the Beiträge, "has confined his occupation with it to pure learning, pure receiving and pondering in the most proper sense of the term, in order to subdue the pampered imagination and finally to drive the old transcendental types out of his head by means of the new rationalist ones", - he now begins the working-over of it in the Beiträge zur leichteren Übersicht des Zustandes der Philosophie beim Anfange des 19.
century.

These Beiträge take up the epoch, so important in the progress of the culture of the human spirit, of the dawn of a new century, to wish it "good fortune, that the occasion of all philosophical revolutions was really discovered no earlier and no later than in the penultimate year of the 18.
century and thereby sublated in the matter itself"65).
As La révolution est finie has been decreed very many times in France, so too has Reinhold already announced several ends of the philosophical revolution.

Now he recognizes the last ending of endings, "although the bad consequences of the transcendental revolution will continue for a considerable time yet", and also adds the question, "whether he is not deceiving himself again now as well? whether nevertheless this true and proper end might after all be only the beginning of a new crooked turn?"66) Rather, the question ought to be put whether this end, however little it is capable of being an end, is capable of being the beginning of anything at all?
zh: 至于赖因霍尔德自己的哲学，他为它给出了一部公开的历史，说他在自己哲学的转世过程中先漫游进了康德哲学，把它脱掉之后进了费希特哲学，从费希特哲学又进了雅可比哲学，而自从他也离开了雅可比哲学之后，就搬进了巴尔迪利的逻辑学。
据《论文集》S. 163，他“把自己的事情限制在纯粹的学习、纯粹的接受和最本己意义上的思索上，为的是压服被惯坏的想象力，并最终用新的理性主义类型把那些旧的先验类型从头脑里赶出去”之后——他现在才开始在《为更容易通观 19
世纪初哲学状况而作的论文集》中加工它。
这些《论文集》抓住人类精神教养进程中那个如此重要的时代，即一个新世纪的破晓，向它祝一声“好运，说一切哲学革命的起因不早不晚，恰好是在 18
世纪真的被发现，并因此在事情本身中得到了扬弃”65)。
正如 La révolution est finie 在法国被无数次地颁令宣布过，赖因霍尔德也已经宣告过哲学革命的好几个终结。
现在他承认了诸终结的最后终结，“尽管先验革命的恶劣后果还会持续相当一段时间”，还加上了这个问题：“他这一次是不是又在骗自己？这个真正的、本己的终结会不会尽管如此又只是一个新的弯折的开端？”66) 其实更应该问的是：这个终结，既然它如此不能成为一个终结，那它究竟能不能成为随便什么东西的开端？

en: For the tendency to ground and to fathom, philosophizing before philosophy, has finally known how to express itself completely.
It has found exactly what was at stake; it is the transformation of philosophy into the formal element of cognition, into logic.
zh: 因为那种论证和深究的倾向，即先于哲学的哲学活动，终于懂得把自己完全说出来了。
它准确地找到了事情的关键所在；这就是把哲学变成认识的形式东西，变成逻辑学。

en: If philosophy as a whole grounds itself and the reality of cognitions according to their form and their content in itself, then by contrast the grounding and fathoming, in its throng of verifying and analysing and of the because and in-so-far-as and then and insofar, comes neither out of itself nor into philosophy.

For the supportless anxiousness, which in its busyness only ever increases, all investigations come too soon, and every beginning is an anticipation, as every philosophy is only a preliminary exercise.

Science claims to ground itself in itself by positing each of its parts absolutely and thereby constituting in the beginning and in each single point an identity and a knowing; as objective totality, knowing grounds itself all the more the more it cultivates itself, and its parts are grounded only simultaneously with this whole of cognitions.

Centre and circle are related to each other in such a way that the first beginning of the circle is already a relation to the centre, and this is not a complete centre unless all its relations, the whole circle, are completed, — a whole that needs a special handle of grounding as little as the earth needs a special handle in order to be grasped by the force that leads it around the sun and at the same time holds it in the whole living manifoldness of its shapes.
zh: 如果哲学作为整体在自身中论证自己以及各种认识在形式和内容上的实在性，那么相反，论证和深究连同它那一堆证实、分析以及“因为”“就……而言”“那么”“只要”，既出不了自身，也进不了哲学。
对于那种毫无支撑的惶恐——它在自己的忙碌中只会不断增长——一切研究都来得太早，每一个开端都是预先插手，正如每一种哲学都只是一次预演。
科学断言自己在自身中论证自己，做法是把它的每一个部分都绝对地设定起来，并由此在开端和每一个别的点上都构成一种同一性和一种知；作为客观的总体性，知越多地培养自己，就同时越多地论证自己，而它的各个部分只有同这个认识的整体一起才得到论证。
中心和圆周这样相互关联：圆周的最初开端已经是对中心的一种关系，而中心若不是它的全部关系、整个圆周都已完成了，就不是一个完整的中心，——这样一个整体，并不比地球更需要一个专门的把手，才能被那股既引领它绕太阳运行、同时又把它保持在它的形态的整个活的杂多中的力量所把握。

en: But grounding occupies itself with always seeking the handle and taking a run-up at living philosophy; it makes this running-up into the true work, and through its principle it makes itself incapable of ever arriving at knowledge and at philosophy.
Logical cognition, if it really goes on as far as reason, must be led to the result that it annihilates itself in reason; it must recognize the antinomy as its highest law.

In Reinhold's theme, the application of thinking, thinking as the infinite repeatability of A as A in A and through A67) does indeed also become antinomical, in that in the application A is, in point of fact, posited as B.
But this antinomy is present quite unconsciously and unacknowledged, for thinking, its application and its material stand peacefully side by side.

Therefore thinking as the faculty of abstract unity, as well as cognition, is merely formal, and the whole grounding is to be only problematic and hypothetical, until in time, in the progress of the problematic and the hypothetical, one comes upon the primally true in the true and upon the true through the primally true68).

But on the one hand this is impossible, for from an absolute formality there is no arriving at any materiality (the two are absolutely opposed), still less at an absolute synthesis, which must be more than a mere joining, - on the other hand, with something hypothetical and problematic, nothing at all is grounded.

Or else cognition is related to the absolute, it becomes an identity of subject and object, of thinking and material; then it is no longer formal, a wretched knowledge has come about, and grounding has once again been missed before knowledge.
For the anxiety of getting into knowledge, nothing remains but to warm itself, with analyzing, methodizing and narrating, at its love and its faith and its goal-directed fixed tendency.
zh: 但论证忙的就是不断去找把手，向活生生的哲学来一次助跑；它把这种助跑变成真正的工作，并且凭自己的原则使自己不可能达到知识和哲学。
逻辑的认识如果真的推进到理性，就必须被引向这样的结果：它在理性中消灭了自己；它必须把二律背反认作自己的最高法则。
在赖因霍尔德的题目，即思维的应用里，思维作为 A 之作为 A 在 A 中并通过 A 的无限可重复性67)，诚然也成了二律背反式的，因为在应用中 A 事实上被设定为 B。
但这个二律背反完全是在无意识、不被承认的情况下存在的，因为思维、它的应用和它的材料和平地并列在一起。
因此，思维作为抽象统一性的能力，以及认识，都只是形式性的，而整个论证也只应是有疑问的和假设的，直到人们随时间推移，在有疑问的东西和假设的东西的进展中，碰上真者里的原初真者，并通过原初真者碰上真者68)。
但一方面这是不可能的，因为从一种绝对的形式性是到不了任何质料性的（两者是绝对对立的），更到不了绝对的综合，而绝对的综合必须多于单纯的接合——另一方面，靠假设的和有疑问的东西，根本就没有论证出任何东西。
或者，认识被联系到绝对者上，它成为主体与客体、思维和材料的同一性；这时它就不再是形式的了，一种令人苦恼的知识产生了，而论证又一次在知识面前落空了。
对于害怕陷入知识的这种恐惧，除了靠分析、方法化和讲述，在它的爱、它的信仰和它那有目标的固定倾向上给自己取暖之外，什么也剩不下。

en: If the run-up does not get across the ditch, then the fault is pushed not onto the perennial persistence of this run-up but onto its method.
But the true method would be the one by which knowing is drawn over, already on this side of the ditch, into the free scope of the run-up itself, and philosophy is reduced to logic.
zh: 如果助跑跨不过那道沟，那么过错就不被推给这种助跑的持久延续，而被推给它的方法。
但真正的方法会是这样一种方法：靠它，知识还在沟的这一边就被拉进助跑自身的活动空间，而哲学则被还原为逻辑。

en: We cannot proceed at once to the consideration of this method by which philosophy is supposed to be transplanted into the domain of the run-up, but must first speak of those presuppositions that Reinhold considers necessary for philosophy, hence of the run-up to the run-up.
zh: 我们不能马上转入对这种方法的考察，据说靠它哲学要被移置到助跑的领域里，而是必须先谈那些赖因霍尔德认为哲学所必需的预设，也就是谈通向助跑的助跑。

en: As the preceding condition of philosophizing, from which the effort to fathom cognition must set out, Reinhold names the love of truth and of certainty; and because this is soon and easily enough acknowledged, Reinhold does not dwell on it any longer.69) And in fact the object of philosophical reflection can be nothing other than the true and the certain.

If consciousness is now filled with this object, then a reflection on the subjective, in the form of a love, has no place in it; it is this reflection that first makes the love, which has an object as sublime as truth is — and no less the individual who, animated by such love, postulates it — into something supremely sublime.
zh: 作为哲学思考的先行条件——穷究认识的努力必须从它出发——，赖因霍尔德举出对真理的爱和对确定性的爱；而因为这一点很快就会轻易得到承认，赖因霍尔德也就不再在它上面多作停留。69) 而事实上，哲学反思的对象只能是真东西和确定的东西。
如果意识现在被这个对象所充满，那么一种以爱的形式对主观东西的反思在其中就没有位置；正是这种反思才首先把爱——它有一个像真理这样崇高的对象——，并且同样把那个为这样的爱所鼓舞、从而提出这种爱的个人，弄成某种极其崇高的东西。

en: The second essential condition of philosophizing, the faith in truth as truth, Reinhold thinks, will not be so easily acknowledged as the love.

Faith would surely have expressed sufficiently what is to be expressed; with regard to philosophy one might perhaps speak of the faith in reason as the genuine health; the superfluousness of the expression "faith in truth as truth", instead of making it more edifying, brings something crooked into it.

The main point is that Reinhold declares in earnest that one should not ask him what the faith in truth is; whoever it is not clear to through itself has and knows no need to find it proved in knowing, which can only proceed from this faith. He does not understand himself in that question;
and Reinhold, then, has nothing further to say to him.70)
zh: 哲学思考的第二个本质条件，即对真理之为真理的信仰，赖因霍尔德认为，不会像爱那样轻易得到承认。
信仰本来就已经足够表达所要表达的东西；就哲学而言，也许可以谈对理性这一真正的健康的信仰；“对真理之为真理的信仰”这个表达的多余，并没有使它更富教益，反倒带进了某种歪斜的东西。
主要之点在于，赖因霍尔德郑重地声明，人们不该问他信仰真理是什么；如果这种信仰不是凭自身就对一个人清楚，那么他就既没有也不认识那种需要，即在知识中证明这种信仰的需要，而知识只能从这种信仰出发。他在那个问题里自己都不理解自己；
而赖因霍尔德也就没有什么更多的话要对他说了。70)

en: If Reinhold believes himself entitled to postulate — then the presupposition of something sublime above all proof, and the right and necessity of postulating that follow from it, are likewise to be found in the postulate of transcendental intuition.

Fichte and Schelling have, after all, as Reinhold himself says, described the peculiar doing of pure reason, transcendental intuition, as an action returning into itself71) ; but Reinhold has nothing at all to say to anyone whom the question about a description of the Reinholdian faith might reach.

But he does more than he believes himself bound to do; he at least determines faith through the opposition to knowing, as a holding-for-true that stands firm through no knowing, and the determination of what knowing is will also show itself in the course of the problematic and hypothetical grounding, as will the common sphere of knowing and faith, and thus the description will complete itself.
zh: 如果赖因霍尔德认为自己有权提出公设——那么，关于某种超乎一切证明之上的东西的预设，以及由此而来的提出公设的权利和必然性，同样也出现在先验直观这一公设里。
费希特和谢林毕竟像赖因霍尔德自己所说的那样，把纯粹理性的独特作为、即先验直观，描述为一种返回自身的行动71)；但对于可能来追问如何描述赖因霍尔德式信仰的人，赖因霍尔德却完全无话可说。
但他所做的多于他自以为有义务做的；他至少通过与知识的对立来规定信仰，把它规定为一种不靠任何知识而确立的信以为真；而对什么是知识的规定，将在这种或然的和假设的论证进程中同样显露出来，知识和信仰的共同领域也会显露出来，于是描述也就变得完整了。

en: If Reinhold believes himself relieved by a postulate of all further saying, then it seems odd to him, on the other hand, that Messrs. Fichte and Schelling postulate; their postulate counts for him as an idiosyncrasy in the consciousness of certain extraordinary individuals equipped with the special sense for it, in whose writings pure reason itself published its acting knowing and its knowing acting.72) Reinhold too believes (S. 143) that he has been in this magic circle, that he has come out of it, and that he now finds himself able to reveal the secret.
